title: What the server does for a storefront request
headline: A warm, cached storefront page is lean (a prerendered home page or a store's own page makes no database read of its own); the cost sits around the page and none of it depends on which features a store uses, so every store pays it once the platform opens. A product page asks the database about 18 times a view where only stock changes per view, the proxy in front of every page loads 1,311 modules (0.8 to 0.95 s and 168 MB cold on this machine) where its five reads need about 50 to 100, and every page load makes a second function call to learn the wishlist is empty and, with a product grid, a third (3 statements) for tile stock that is off by default. Cached pages are drawn again by the clock (1 hour for 71 of 85 cached reads, 15 minutes for the home page), by every deploy (up to 52 on 11 Nov) and by any one owner saving AI settings, which expires every store's pages (319 of the build's 1,316 prerendered entries carry that one tag). Nothing here removes or hides a feature: 16 fixes make cost follow use, five of them small and safe enough to do first, and before opening is the cheapest time for all of them.

Stock is the one catalogue fact read per request by design, and the rule is written (docs/rules/storefront.md:110-114). Every fix here keeps it.

Checked by the verifier and not a server cost: the 5,200 repeated RSC requests on a category page of the local build come from the browser's cache (88 KB transferred in all). That loop belongs to the client dimension.

findings.title: The proxy and every storefront page load about half of the server's code at cold start
findings.evidence: My walk of value imports from src/proxy.ts reaches 1,311 modules, 20.6 MB of source (483 server files, 813 lib files, the schema). Loading the built proxy in a fresh node process took 920 and 948 ms and added 167 to 168 MB (the verifier: 795 to 840 ms; the bare libraries 133 to 172 ms). What the proxy calls is small: five readers. They sit in files that also hold writers, so the imports of those writers come along. The proxy reaches auth.ts three ways (holding.ts:9 for audit(), house-switch.ts:8, not-found.ts:24 through permissions.ts), pages.ts, stores.ts and seo.ts through house-switch.ts:11-17, catalog.ts through redirect-resolve.ts:19 for one tag function, redirects.ts for countHit (redirect-resolve.ts:23, not-found.ts:26), and page-content.ts (197 KB) through experiments.ts. Cutting those 16 import edges leaves 97 modules and 1.95 MB (52 and 0.5 MB once db/client.ts:11 drops the schema). For the page functions: the store layout reaches 1,466 modules; 1,011 without customers.ts:17 -> privacy-erasure.ts. The third named cut is wider than reported: admin-text.ts (every admin catalogue, 147 files, 3.7 MB) is imported by 8 files on this path, not one. With only two-step.ts changed the layout still reaches 999 and the proxy 830; the verified 872 and 702 need all eight (two-step.ts and seven server modules, five of which want the staffEmails area alone).
findings.cost: About 0.8 to 0.95 s and 168 MB each time a proxy instance starts cold (this machine, not Vercel), before any page on any host, static pages included. Cold starts come with each new instance and each deploy (up to 52 on 11 Nov). A cold page function loads the same knot (the verifier: the store page's page.js alone 310 to 331 ms, a lower bound). The 12 proxy runs of one home view are warm and do not each pay this.
findings.who_pays: A shopper's first byte on a cold instance; the server's memory and compute. The same for every store, whatever it uses.

findings.title: A product page asks the database about 18 times per view; one answer changes per view
findings.evidence: Measured again: one anonymous GET of the prerendered /s/demo/no/p/demo-keramikkopp on the warm local build committed 20 times in a window whose idle floor is 1. Tables read: inventory_levels, inventory_locations and inventory_reservations +8 each (stock is read by the buy part at product-parts.tsx:1012 and again by the JSON-LD part at :694), payment_providers +7, shipping_rates +4, checkout_providers +2 and vat_rates +2 (getCheckoutInfo() runs in expressOn() and in klarnaMessaging(), express-checkout.ts:62 and :155), platform_settings +2 (getCheckoutUi() at :61 and :155), price_breaks +2, and automations, order_settings, checkout_fields, payment_methods and stripe_accounts +1 each. None of these readers is cached. priceBreaksFor() runs for a guest too (price-breaks.ts:17-18 has no early return for a null customer; listPricesFor() at price-lists.ts:459 has one). The buy part waits in rounds before the button is drawn: the scheme check (:997), quote mode (:1001), the wave at :1011-1020 through a pool of 5 connections, then Klarna's states (express-checkout.ts:158). Every one of these runs for every store, whether or not it uses express checkout, Klarna, back in stock, quotes, price breaks, checkout questions or producer schemes. Next's guide says a cached read called at request time on serverless typically does not persist across requests, so the fix must carry the facts in the prerendered page, not in an instance's memory.
findings.cost: About 16 statements beyond the proxy's per product view. It grows one for one with shopper traffic, on the page where the buy button is: the largest per-request cost on the storefront once the platform opens.
findings.who_pays: The server and the database per request; the shopper waits on 'Checking stock' for the buy button.
fix_steps: Step 1, safe and alone worth shipping: share within one request through perRequest() (src/server/request-memo.ts:13-20). getVariantStock() keyed by the store and the sorted ids (src/server/catalog.ts:566-569; its callers at product-parts.tsx:694 and :1012 then share one read), getCheckoutUi() (src/server/connect.ts:476-479) and getCheckoutInfo() when no view is passed (src/server/orders.ts:520). Expected: about 18 to about 15.

Step 2: new src/server/buy-facts.ts with buyFacts(storeId, marketCode): 'use cache', cacheLife("hours"), cacheTag(buyTag(storeId), catalogTag(storeId), BUY_PLATFORM_TAG). One statement returns what only owners and the platform change: checkout_ui; payments on, the active mode and whether checkout is Mollie's (the three expressions of orders.ts:522-541); the account id for the mode (settings.ts:110-118); whether Klarna is switched off for the market (payment_methods) and its state (stripe_accounts.method_states); whether an enabled checkout field exists; order_settings.quote_requests; whether the back_in_stock automation is enabled; whether the store has any price_breaks or price_list_breaks row; whether it has any product_schemes row. What depends on the environment (platformModes(), mollieAppOn(), platformPublishableKey()) is applied in code after the read, never cached.

Step 3: refreshBuyFacts(storeId) (refreshTag(buyTag(storeId))) is called by each writer of those tables: setStripeProvider (src/server/settings.ts:77), the stripe_accounts writes of src/server/connect.ts (refreshStripeAccount and the host's), src/server/mollie.ts, saveMethodChoices in src/server/payment-methods.ts, the checkout_fields writers in src/server/checkout-rules.ts, the order_settings writers (order-settings.ts, quote-requests.ts, draft-orders.ts, suppliers.ts), the automation switch in src/server/automations.ts, and products.ts and price-lists.ts where they write breaks or schemes. setCheckoutUi (connect.ts:482) refreshes BUY_PLATFORM_TAG.

Step 4: a scan test, src/server/buy-writers.scan.test.ts, in the style of src/server/store-writers.scan.test.ts: a file that writes one of those tables calls refreshBuyFacts( or is on a list that only shrinks.

Step 5: the product page reads the facts with its other cached reads, src/app/s/[store]/[market]/p/[handle]/page.tsx:126-136, and puts them in ctx.buy (ProductPageContext, product-parts.tsx:96-107, optional). ProductPartView hands ctx.buy to VariantsWithStock (:275, :287). The facts are then part of the prerendered page and cost nothing per view, also on a fresh instance.

Where ctx.buy is absent (the admin's layout preview) they read as today.

Step 7: the cart's drawing (src/app/s/[store]/[market]/cart/cart-contents.tsx:159-160) may use the same facts. The press itself (cart/actions.ts:428) keeps its live expressOn() read, and startCheckout() keeps its own checks.

findings.title: Every deploy empties the caches and nothing warms them
findings.evidence: Only the template store is prerendered at build (prerenderedShops(), shop.ts:93-100); the fallback shell for any other store is a 0-byte file (.next/server/app/s/[store]/[market].html), so its first visit after a deploy is drawn whole at request time. Next's guide: all cache stores 'are scoped to a single deployment. A new deploy starts fresh', and neither caching directive carries over to a new deploy. 90 commits were made on 11 Nov; the verifier found 52 of 89 touched code, and such a push deploys. await-deploy.mjs waits for /api/health and calls two API refusals (SMOKE_CHECKS, :52-56), then stops: it requests no page. docs/performance.md:84 records a page that took 3.1 s to answer while a deploy went live.
findings.cost: Today the team and crawlers meet the cold pages. After opening, the first visitor to each page of each store after each deploy waits for a cold function start (SD-1) plus about 30 statements (SD-5). Cold draws are stores x visited pages x deploys a day, so it grows with both the store count and the present habit of many deploys a day. Not timed in production.
findings.who_pays: Shoppers (first byte) and owners looking at their store after a change, once the platform is open; the database for each cold draw.
fix_steps: Step 1, now: scripts/await-deploy.mjs:52-56 gains page checks. After production reports the commit it requests Kaizena Flow's home and one page of the template store (addresses from a new SMOKE_PAGES variable set in .github/workflows/ci.yml beside PRODUCTION_URL), each expecting 200. Read from the code; not measured with cookies.
findings.cost: 1 extra statement per view for a shopper with a cart; 2 to 4 extra on a product page for a signed-in shopper. It grows with real shoppers, who do not exist yet.
findings.who_pays: The database per request; the shoppers closest to buying.

Step 2: getCartCount(shop) (src/server/cart.ts:544-556) the same, keyed by store and market.
Step 3: src/server/visibility.ts:62 calls getCustomer() directly and drops its own key.

findings.title: The browser's side has budgets; the server's side has none that can see these costs

The one server-side number is the first byte of two warm store pages, under 250 ms (e2e/performance.spec.ts:127-130; measured under 10 ms). It cannot see any finding here: the shell answers first and the statements run in the stream after it. Nothing counts the proxy's import graph (1,311 modules), a page's statements per view (about 18 on a product page), what a page load asks for after the document (SD-14, SD-15), that a cached read sets a life and a tag (2 set no life), or that a store's action refreshes only that store's tags (SD-16). The import walk and the statement count used in this review are each a few lines, in the style of tests the repository already has.
findings.cost: No bytes today. It is why SD-1, SD-2, SD-8, SD-14, SD-15 and SD-16 could grow unseen, and they will grow faster once real stores switch features on.
findings.who_pays: Everyone later: shoppers, the server, the database.

findings.title: Product tiles ask the server for stock on every page load, also in stores that show none
findings.evidence: The store's two switches (stock on tiles, Add to cart on tiles) are off until an owner turns them on (DEFAULT_PRODUCT_SETTINGS, shop-tiles.ts:21). A grid's own choice is absent by default and means 'follow the store', so tileAsk() returns an ask for every product grid (shop-tiles.ts:35-39) and each tile mounts an island that fetches /api/shop/tiles (tile-shop.tsx:33). Only when the answer arrives does the browser learn the store's settings and draw nothing (tileShows(), tile-shop.tsx:55). The route reads the settings, then every named product's variants, then their stock, whatever the settings say (src/server/shop-tiles.ts:27, :30-51, :52). Measured on the local build: the demo store has no product_settings row; its home page and All products each made the call (routes.json); one call for its 10 products read product_settings +1, products +33, product_variants +67, inventory_levels +32, inventory_locations +13, inventory_reservations +16 and bundle_components +240, and committed 4 statements over the idle floor (3 by the code). The answer began {"settings":{"tileStock":false,"tileQuantity":false}, so nothing was drawn.
findings.cost: Per load of a page with a product grid, in every store that has not switched the feature on: one function call, 3 statements (one of them the stock of every product on the page) and an answer nobody uses. It grows one for one with page loads of home and listing pages.
findings.who_pays: The server and the database per page load; the shopper's browser (one request and the island's script).
fix_steps: Step 1, keeps D557 as written: tileFacts() (src/server/shop-tiles.ts:23-29) returns { settings, facts: {}, buttons } right after reading the settings when both are off and no grid of the page asks on its own. The island adds own=1 to its request when an ask holds 'show' (src/components/tile-shop.tsx:21-41; the batch keeps it if any tile says so) and the route passes it on (src/app/api/shop/tiles/route.ts:17-27). Saves 2 of the 3 statements.

Step 2, removes the call: src/server/product-settings.ts gains a cached tileSettings(storeId) ('use cache', cacheLife("hours"), cacheTag(productSettingsTag(storeId))), and saveProductSettings() (:27-37) refreshes that tag with refreshTag(). src/components/content-grid-section.tsx:37 and :139 resolve the ask on the server with a new pure tileAskFor(own, settings) in src/lib/shop-tiles.ts, which is null when tileShows() would be false for both; ContentGridView then draws no island (content-grid.tsx:81). The route still reads the settings and the stock per request, so stock is never cached and a switch turned off stops showing at once.

Step 3: the rule's words. docs/rules/admin/website.md:728 and the header of src/lib/shop-tiles.ts:6-8 say that the store's settings decide whether the island is drawn (cached under their own tag) and that the route still answers them with the facts. The comment at product-settings.ts:13-16 ('never in a use cache function') gets its reason kept: a change must not refresh the catalogue, and a tag of its own keeps that.
tests_and_rules: src/lib/shop-tiles.test.ts (tileAsk and tileShows; add tileAskFor).

findings.title: One owner saving AI settings expires the cached pages of every store
findings.evidence: The chat button's cached read carries one tag for the whole platform, 'ai-providers' (ai.ts:242, chat-agent.ts:138). The market layout draws that read on every page, so every prerendered store page carries the tag: 319 of the build's 1,316 prerendered entries do, the template store's home, product and text pages and Kaizena Flow's own home among those I opened. A store owner's own action refreshes that tag: saveStoreAiAction and removeStoreAiAction call updateTag(AI_TAG) (settings/ai/actions.ts:34 and :50). Next's guide on updateTag: it 'immediately expires the cached data', and 'the next request will wait to fetch fresh data'. So one owner saving their own AI key expires every page of every other store, and of Kaizena Flow's site, at once. The store pages carry one more platform-wide tag, 'catalog'; only the platform's VAT tools refresh that one (vat-admin.ts:39-41, :345, :372), and that is tracked as FF3.
findings.cost: Per save of AI settings by any owner: every visited page of every store is drawn cold on its next visit (about 30 statements each, SD-5) and that visitor waits for it. It grows with stores x pages x owners who touch the setting. Today nobody notices: the stores are the team's.
findings.who_pays: Shoppers of other stores (first byte after the flush); the server and the database for the redraws.
fix_steps: Step 1: src/server/ai.ts:242 gains aiTag(storeId) = `ai:${storeId ?? "kaizen"}`; AI_TAG stays only as the platform's, aiTag(null).

Step 2: src/server/chat-agent.ts:138 tags the widget with chatTag(storeId), aiTag(storeId) and aiTag(null): a store without a provider of its own answers with Kaizena Flow's (ai.ts:200-211), so the platform's tag stays on its pages.

Step 3: saveAiSettings() and removeAiSettings() in src/server/ai.ts (the only writers of commerce.ai_providers, by rg) refresh aiTag(storeId) themselves with refreshTag(); src/app/admin/(gated)/[store]/settings/ai/actions.ts:34 and :50 drop updateTag(AI_TAG). The platform's actions (platform/ai/actions.ts:52, :66) and src/server/docs-guide-settings.ts:137 use aiTag(null).
Step 4: hold it with the scan of SD-13 step 2: no file under src/app/admin/(gated)/[store] refreshes a tag from the list of platform-wide tags.
